typical_symptoms: Skeletonized leaf tissue with main veins remaining intact
Chewed fruit structures including squares and bolls
Presence of larvae actively feeding on foliage
Accumulation of dark frass pellets on leaf surfaces
visual_characteristics: Caterpillars with prominent longitudinal dark and cream-colored stripes
Distinct dark triangular markings along the dorsolateral sides of larvae
Ragged and missing leaf sections with uneven, chewed margins
Reddish-brown to orange head capsules on feeding caterpillars
lesion_characteristics: Irregular chew holes with jagged, torn margins
Absence of chlorotic halos around cut tissue
Desiccated tan to light brown rims on freshly chewed leaf edges
Size ranges from small windowpane nibbles to complete leaf blade consumption
color_characteristics: Larvae vary from light green to dark brown or black with yellowish longitudinal lines
Damaged leaf margins desiccate to pale tan or medium brown
Frass pellets range from dark green to brown-black
texture_characteristics: Rough and jagged chewed foliage edges
Smooth to slightly velvety larval bodies
Dry, papery residual leaf tissue left by early instar feeding
spatial_patterns: Irregularly scattered defoliation across upper and lower canopy leaves
Random holes in foliage expanding outward from initial feeding sites
Localized heavy feeding spots where larval clusters aggregate
distinguishing_features: Presence of live striped caterpillars on the plant foliage
Mechanical chewing damage rather than pathogen-induced necrotic spots
Dark frass deposits visible on leaf surfaces beneath active feeding sites
